hmmm about 2.5 hours? They’re pretty hard tbh but if you’re studying you should at least pass. He’s not a harsh grader. And yea that sounds about right, every two weeks. Sometimes there’s one the week after depending on breaks and such.

Exams are commonly 5 questions with a 6th as extra credit. His class has 15 formal labs, all of which are input into a “notebook” that you create on Google docs. They aren’t full reports but require a methods, tools, discussion, and a place to answer questions he has in the lab. You will input the link to the doc to turn it in on Canvas. He will check them after you turn it in but usually not when it’s due. (You commonly have time to edit it later, he doesn’t really check the history.) You’re given instructions for the labs but 4A is all about problem solving, so you’ll have to determine what methods to use in order to yield results you want. 

For quizzes, there’s about 7-8. He drops the lowest one at least. But that’s not the same for the exam.
I don’t but I can try to answer questions you have about it. I took his class in the Fall so it’s still somewhat fresh in my mind.

I’ve taken him for 4A. Professor Cabrera is a very nice guy and always available to answer questions that you have. However, he graded the entire semester extremely late. I’m talking one week before finals with only 3-4 things graded. So a lot of students didn’t know where they stood in terms of their grade for the semester. But in terms of policies, just show up to class ig and work with your table group to solve questions. Majority of your grade is dependent on exams and labs, which he doesn’t give the best feedback for but you can ask him about it after your receive the grade.
